answer: A slashable-stake registry makes identity expensive: each agent locks collateral before it can vote or earn, and a random beacon picks agents to prove control of a unique key. A Sybil attacker who clones one program across a nebula of fake nodes must post a separate bond for every island identity they create. If two identities wander with the same key, both get slashed. The cost to the attacker is N bonds at risk, so multiplying identities multiplies capital, not just reach.
